solution_sketch: Factor each term: 1 - 1/k^2 = (k-1)(k+1)/k^2. The product splits into two telescoping chains, prod (k-1)/k = 1/10 and prod (k+1)/k = 11/2. Their product is (1/10)(11/2) = 11/20. In general prod_{k=2}^{n}(1-1/k^2) = (n+1)/(2n); here n=10 gives 11/20.
difficulty_rationale: Naive route: compute nine fractions 3/4, 8/9, 15/16, ... and multiply them, punishing without paper. Insight: each factor is (k-1)(k+1)/k^2, so numerators and denominators cancel across neighbours. After the insight there are still real steps: recognise the two telescoping chains, evaluate their surviving ends (1/10 and 11/2), and multiply. More than a single 20s move but under 40s.
